items.title: Lee Robinson: four technical bets
items.summary: No UI, thin client / thick server, always-on computer, browser as a first-class tool.
items.text:
Grok @Bot has made a few simple yet powerful technical decisions that I believe make it easy and enjoyable to use.

1. The best UI is none at all. The product interface is dramatically simpler than alternatives without sacrificing functionality. How is this possible? It's one of the first products designed for current frontier model capabilities and has a UI restrained enough to remain easy to use as models improve exponentially. Everyone knows how to text.

2. A thin harness for the client, a thick harness for the server. You might have noticed the app feels very fluid to use, even for a beta product. This is primarily because of everything we didn't have to build. The app harness is essentially a single tool to send messages between the client and server. The complexity moves to the server, where you can still use the coding agent harness with specialized tools as needed. This helps make the UI fast and responsive on desktop and mobile.

3. An always-on computer. Most coding agents and assistants today start fresh with every question you ask. Some of these sessions are on your local machine and others happen in the cloud. We believe strongly that cloud is the future, which is why it's the only option. Further, rather than spinning up virtual machines for every conversation, your bots connect to their own computer. This means you can still run agents on the bot's persistent filesystem. It's closer to what programmers have been doing by using Tailscale from their phones to connect to a remote computer and run an agent TUI. You get those capabilities without the hassle.

4. Your bots can use the browser. Coding agents have shown that most work on a computer can be expressed and run as code. You can ask for a task in natural language and the agent will decide to write a script to complete it. This is amazing, but there's still many tasks which can't be completed without logging into a website and clicking around the browser. Models and harnesses are now good enough to reliably handle this. The combination of writing code and using browsers means you can automate almost any task on a computer. Further, you can ask Grok Bot to record you doing the task, and then turn it into something repeatable.

items.title: Danny Limanseta: 74 game art assets in two hours
items.summary: Bot reads the codebase, hits his art-gen page, crops transparent PNGs, and wires 74 card assets back into the game.
items.text:
I’ve been using Grok Bot in early access for a little over a week now, and it has been a massive boost to my game dev workflow and my productivity in general.

One of the first things I asked it to do was to visit my custom art generation tool webpage and generate art assets to replace all the image placeholders in my game.

It looked through my codebase to understand what each asset was, wrote a custom art generation prompt for every single one, generated the images, cropped and cleaned them up into transparent PNGs, and then wired them back into the game.

In about 2 hours, it generated 74 (cleaned and cropped) art assets for the cards and integrated all of them into my game. Now, ALL my art assets workflows go through Grok bot.

This blew my mind because, before this, I was doing everything manually, one asset at a time. It basically solved my entire art asset workflow and allowed me to put it on autopilot, which is amazing.

I’ve also been using Grok Bot for:

Playtesting my game: The bot was a little slow initially, so I asked it to build a skill specifically designed to playtest my game, with intimate knowledge of its rules and mechanics. It’s much faster now, though I’m still looking for ways to optimise its speed.

Setting up my itchio page for my game: It also automated a workflow that uploads a new build to itch whenever I push one to GitHub. Going to the itch website and uploading builds manually every single time was always a pain.

Flowcharts and UX design: I’m a UX designer by day, so I decided to give it a much bigger task. I fed the agent a PRD and asked it to design the UX flows and wireframes. With the help of the Figma MCP, it actually delivered.

Auditing all my paid subscriptions: I had it go through my emails and hunt down subscriptions that I might have forgotten about.

Unsubscribing me from marketing newsletters: It did this beautifully, though it did miss a few newsletters.

What I’ve learned is that it takes time to discover all the possible use cases for Grok bot. I’ve had to reevaluate my day-to-day workflows and figure out which parts I can delegate to it.

So far, it has been a huge productivity unlock for me and I am discovering more uses for my Grok bots every other day.

items.title: Kaspa node density test on one Grok Bot box
items.summary: Honest one-sandbox density notes measuring how many real Kaspa mainnet public nodes a single Grok Bot Linux box can run.
items.text: > Experimental only. Not a product. > > Do not use wallet integrations on this GitHub. STP remains a clown. DISCLAIMER.md
outline: Official rusty-kaspa kaspad ran on the Grok Bot box. There was one archival primary and a fleet of non-archival slots.
Each fleet slot used low peer caps, its own ports, and its own bore tunnel so it was reachable from outside.
Slots were launched until free memory reached a floor. Then the test stopped, and only nodes that were really alive and reachable were counted. No fake peers or…
The Testnet-10 node on the same box was protected and not counted.
RAM: ~15 GiB shared, and swap is not available on the sandbox.
Shared compute: the archival primary, TN10 and the agent runtimes already use most of the machine.
IBD balloon: a syncing kaspad grows from tens of MB to 1–2 GiB, even at --ram-scale=0.1, which is the lowest value kaspad accepts.
Ephemeral /tmp: a box wipe loses the datadirs, and the nodes have to sync from scratch again.

items.text: Finbot is a two-tier accumulation engine designed for disciplined long-term accumulation of high-conviction holdings (IBM, QTUM, and AIPO). It is not a short-term swing-trading system: there are no 1.5× ATR stops and no 2R/3R profit targets. Instead, it identifies optimal technical confluence windows for adding buy tranches into structural pullbacks when the underlying fundamental thesis is already established.
outline: Daily Webhook Snapshot — On every scan, POSTs full ticker JSON (gates, technical indicators, asset archetype, earnings status, tranche levels) to Grok Bot web…

IBM (asset_type: equity) — Core enterprise AI/hybrid cloud dividend compounder. Subject to single-name earnings blackouts.
QTUM (asset_type: etf) — Defiance Quantum ETF (~70 equal-weighted tech/quantum holdings). Earnings blackout marked N/A.
AIPO (asset_type: etf) — Defiance AI & Power Infrastructure ETF (grid, nuclear, data center utilities). Surfaces indicator maturity status.
Philosophy: Standard institutional accumulation into minor consolidations during established uptrends.
Trend Requirement: 50 SMA is upward-sloping (SMA50[t] > SMA50[t - 10]) and close is within −1.5% to +3.0% of the 50 SMA.
Pullback Requirement: Daily RSI 14 pulled back into the 35 to 48 consolidation zone.

css/style.css; js/core.js (helpers, renderer), js/roles.js, js/world.js, js/daynight.js, js/agents.js, js/panels.js, js/minimap.js, js/ui.js,

items.text: 這個 repo 收錄我和 Grok Bot 一起做的所有專案。每個專案一個資料夾，各自有 README，並且都能直接透過 GitHub Pages 線上試玩。 *A showroom of every project I build with Grok Bot — one folder per project, each with its own README and a live GitHub Pages demo.*
outline: YYYYMMDD 是專案的開始日期（台北時間），所以資料夾會依時間先後自然排序。*The date is the project's start date, so folders sort chronologically.
用小寫英文與連字號，例如 orbital-forge。*Lowercase, hyphenated slug.
同一專案後續的改版放在同一個資料夾內（例如舊版放進 v1/ 子資料夾），不另開新資料夾。*Later versions stay in the same folder (older versions in sub-folders such as v1/).

新增專案時：建立資料夾 → 放入 index.html 與 README.md → 在上方表格與根目錄 index.html 加一列。*To add a project: new folder, add it to this table and to the root index.html.

items.title: grokbot-home — move a whole Grok Bot fleet to a new account
items.summary: One user's public "home" repo for switching Grok Bot accounts: a Bot on the new account reads BOOTSTRAP.md, asks for a passphrase to decrypt the Composio key, installs tools, then recreates every other Bot from saved profiles, memories and routines with CreateAgent and writes what it learned back.
items.text: 我的 Grok Bot「家」：换到新的 Grok Bot 账号时，让新号上的 bot 按这个仓库把自己和其他所有 bot 一起配好，做到基本无缝切换。
outline: （Step 0）匿名克隆本仓库 → 用密码框（secret-request）向我要口令 GROKBOT_HOME_PASSPHRASE → 解密 secrets/COMPOSIO_API_KEY.enc 到 ~/.composio_pg_key（连不上就换 .box-current.enc）→ 从 c
（Step 1）用 Composio 里 GitHub（ZMGID）的 token 登录 gh——只有往仓库推送（写回、每日同步）才需要；
跑 setup.sh 装好工具环境（KiCad、PlatformIO、cadquery、Composio SDK 等）；
确认 composio-pg 已接通；pstack 插件可选（原为 dr eggbot 安装）；导入 skills/ 里的技能（若有）；
按 bots/grok-bot/ 设置自己为 小萌（主 bot；原名 Grok Bot）并读 CONTEXT.md；
用 CreateAgent 把 bots/ 下其他每个 bot（小枳、仓库管家、代码工程师、搭建运维、事务秘书、硬件工程师……，以 bots/index.json 为准）重新建出来，并重建它们的定时任务；
自检，最后把新学到的东西写回仓库。
仓库是公开的，明文密钥永远不进仓库。唯一例外是 secrets/*.enc：用 scripts/secret-crypt.py 加密后的 Composio key。口令只通过 bot 的密码框（secret prompt）给，绝不写进仓库或聊天。推送前必须 bash scripts/secret-scan

items.title: Prime Directive — a two-Bot coding team where only you merge
items.summary: Playbook and two shared Grok Bot templates, Builder Prime and Gatekeeper Prime, for a coding team in which one Bot builds, the other reviews and nothing merges without the human's approval, with setup and how-it-works guides.
items.text: Prime Directive
outline: Plan (big work only). For a new subsystem, anything security-related, or roughly 400+ changed lines, Builder Prime writes a short plan and Gatekeeper Prime OK…
Build. Builder Prime branches, codes, tests, and opens a PR that says what changed, why, and where any reused ideas came from.
Prove the fix. Every bug fix ships with a test that fails on main and passes on the PR.
Review. Gatekeeper Prime reads the full diff at the head commit, runs the risky paths, and posts a public review with ranked findings and a verdict.
Fix and re-review. Builder Prime pushes fixes to the same branch. Gatekeeper Prime re-reads what actually changed. It never takes "fixed" on faith.
Your call. You get a short note: PR, commit, checks green, one line on why. Say yes and it squash-merges, locked to exactly the commit you approved.
Public reviews, pinned to the commit. Every review goes on the PR itself and names the exact head SHA it covers. If you build in the open, the review should b…
Every fix proves itself. A bug or security fix comes with a regression test that fails on main and passes on the PR. The reviewer runs it against main to

items.title: Next Mission — Grok Bot template files for U.S. military transition
items.summary: Shared files for the Next Mission Grok Bot template that helps U.S. service members who are retiring or separating, including a sourced master checklist by time to separation, state veteran benefits and scripts that check sourcing and build a personal deadline list.
items.text: This repository holds the shared files for the Next Mission Grok Bot template, an assistant for U.S. service members who are retiring or separating from active duty.
outline: MASTER_CHECKLIST.md is a starter checklist for service members who are retiring or separating. It is organized by how much time is left before the separation
STATE_BENEFITS.md lists state veteran benefits. It currently covers Texas and Oklahoma, and it explains how to research and add another state using the same r…
check_checklist.py and check_state_benefits.py check the sourcing rules in the two Markdown files.
deadlines.py builds a personal deadline list from the checklist and a profile file, and lists free perks you can claim now or soon.
compare_versions.py lists the checklist rows that changed between a saved previous copy and the current copy, by row ID, old value versus new value, filtered
profile.example.json is an example profile with an explanation of every field.
test_profiles/ holds three made-up profiles used for testing the scripts. They do not describe real people, and a normal install does not need them.
VERSION holds the date of the checklist's last full check.

items.text: Feature request for product/service – Other – Describe the request Please add a per-agent “reasoning effort” control in Bot / chat settings — for example low / mid / full, or a way to dial down (or skip) deep reasoning on agents that do not need it. Today it feels like everyone gets the heavy path by default, which slows group / table chats and burns weekly usage on seats that only needed a quick turn. Voice already feels like a stripped-down, faster path — so the capability is clearly there. Exposing the same kind of knob for text / multi-agent chat would make multi-bot conversations snappier and more natural, and stretch the weekly allowance further. Concrete ask …

items.title: Grok Bot reconnect loop — api2.cursor.sh bad cert host
items.summary: Grok Bot stuck on “Can’t reach your computer” because api2.cursor.sh resolves to 100.60.17.13 serving a mismatched certificate.
items.text: Where does the bug appear (feature/product)? Grok Bot Describe the Bug Grok Bot stays on “Can’t reach your computer” and keeps reconnecting. Cursor’s updater says the certificate is invalid and the server may be pretending to be api2[.]cursor[.]sh. api2[.]cursor[.]sh CNAMEs to api2geo[.]cursor[.]sh, then api2direct[.]cursor[.]sh. Both 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 return 100.60.17.13 in that set. Connecting to 100.60.17.13 with that hostname presents a certificate for devapi[.]english[.]com (Pearson PLC / Sectigo), so TLS hostname verification fails. From the same network, 34.235.15.195 in the same DNS set presents the correct certificate (CN=api2[.]cursor[.]sh, issuer Amazon RSA 2048 M01). Mobile hotspot works because it gets a different address list. No local proxy or antivirus HTTPS scanning. Changing DNS to 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 does not remove 100.60.17.13. Steps to Reproduce …

items.text: Introducing Grok Bot Blog · Docs · Get started Today we’re launching Grok Bot in early beta: AI teammates you can give real work to. Bots sign in to the tools you already use and work in them just like you do, on a persistent cloud computer with a browser, filesystem, and terminal. They finish jobs end to end and only come back when something needs your approval. You work with a Bot like you would a teammate. Give it a task, shut your computer, and pick the thread back up from desktop or iOS. What’s new: • A computer of its own: Bots work on a persistent cloud computer that keeps their files and logins, with connectors and MCP where available, and computer use everywhere else, so work lands in the real tool, not a draft you have to move. • Bots that coordinate with each other: Your Bots share one computer, and each gets its own screen, so several can work in parallel. …

items.text: Feature request for product/service Cursor IDE Describe the request Cursor IDE — Grok Bot Official docs say not to use separate Bots as a security boundary. That’s correct, and it’s the gap. Several Bots share one cloud computer and one Chrome. chrome://settings/content/all shows hosts and storage, not which account. A cookie-host list is not an inventory. Any Bot can use a session another Bot signed in (example: a site signed in as the human’s Workspace account). What exists today: approval cards, Auto-review (Require / Always Allow), delete-the-bot. Persona text that says “read-only” is not a lock. What’s needed: • A signed-in dashboard: Account | Site, grouped by identity. Not cookie hostnames. • Per-Bot browser profiles / credential isolation, or an explicit “this session is usable by Bot X only.” …

I recently noticed that simply logging into GrokBot appears to affect Cursor’s “Too many computers” protection. What surprised me is that I did not send any messages or start any Agent tasks through GrokBot. I only completed the login. So I’d like to understand: Does Cursor officially treat GrokBot as a separate computer/device? If so, I think this behavior should be documented much more clearly. Before logging in, there was no indication that GrokBot would count as another device, no warning that the login could affect the device limit, and no way to see how many devices Cursor currently recognizes. This is particularly confusing for developers who regularly use multiple environments and integrations. …

items.title: No compact / new session; full transcript is sent each turn
items.summary: Staff: desktop and iOS have no explicit Compact or same-bot new session. Auto-summary is not compact; the full transcript is sent, and there is no model picker.
items.text: Describe the request We are rewriting the app around this. We need you to ship the primitives so a Bot is an object, not an unbounded thread. Problem Each Bot is one unbounded thread. Every turn reloads the full transcript (user messages, agent messages, tool dumps, screenshots, agent-to-agent pings). Obsolete traffic stays in the model context forever. There is no same-agent “new session,” no compact, and no way for the Bot to drop dead messages from what the model sees. The documented workaround is spawn another Bot. That explodes the roster, splits memory, and does not fix the product. Rewrite (what we are building against) • Split a Bot into Identity, Working set, Archive. Stop treating the chat log as the Bot. • Identity = name, description, memory, routines, skills, connectors. Survives forever. …

items.title: Grok Bot Zoom plugin OAuth hardcodes http://localhost:8787/callback — Zoom rejects hostname localhost (error 4700)
items.summary: Staff: the catalog Zoom plugin OAuth hardcodes http://localhost:8787/callback, which Zoom rejects (error 4700); no user workaround until the redirect moves off localhost (e.g. 127.0.0.1).
items.text: Where does the bug appear (feature/product)? Grok Bot Describe the Bug When connecting the catalog Zoom plugin from Grok Bot, OAuth always starts with redirect_uri=http://localhost:8787/callback. Zoom rejects the hostname localhost with error 4700 (Invalid redirect / « Redirection non valide ») and Zoom Marketplace will not even let you add localhost to the OAuth allow list (« localhost is not allowed »; Zoom only accepts http://127.0.0.1 or http://[::1] for loopback, or HTTPS otherwise). Grok Bot has no parameter to change the redirect URI. Recreating the Zoom Marketplace app does not help: Cursor still sends localhost. items.title: Status beat leaks between bots — one Bot memory across 1:1 and groups
items.summary: Staff (Colin): Status “leaks” across chats are expected—each Bot has one conversation and one memory spanning its 1:1 and every group it joins; group turns are room-tagged but memories belong to the Bot, so keep Project X and Y on separate Bots (or file notes under a project folder, which is less reliable than separate Bots).
items.text: Where does the bug appear (feature/product)? Grok Bot Describe the Bug Two separate Grok Bot chats/bots are using the same underlying agent for different long-running research projects. Project A is running in one bot/chat, while Project B is running in a separate bot/chat. Both projects require regular status beats every few minutes, reporting what was found and including a link. The problem: progress from one project shows up in the other bot/chat. Because both bots share the same underlying agent, durable memory and conversation history contain information from both projects. A status beat for Project B keeps Project B “hot,” so the next turn in the separate bot/chat often answers with Project B findings instead of the findings for that bot’s own project. The two bots are separate conversation surfaces, but they are backed by the same agent ID. …

items.title: Windows instant crash — Codex sandbox ACL missing S-1-15-2-2
items.summary: Staff (deanrie, 2026-09-05): Quiet Windows launch crash (int3 / 0x80000003) is often AppData\Local install ACLs left by CodexSandboxUsers without ALL RESTRICTED APPLICATION PACKAGES (S-1-15-2-2)—`--disable-gpu`/`--jitless` won’t help; diagnose with `--disable-gpu-sandbox`, then `icacls` grant S-1-15-2-1/2 (RX) on the Grok Bot folder (and optionally `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`) or remove the orphaned
items.text: Where does the bug appear (feature/product)? Grok Bot Describe the Bug Grok Bot crashes on every launch, about 1 second after start, before any UI appears. 1–3 processes flash in Task Manager and vanish. No window, no error dialog. 100% reproducible. The GPU child process exits with code -2147483645 (STATUS_BREAKPOINT / 0x80000003). The whole app then tears down. WinDbg on the Crashpad dump shows a literal int3 (0xCC) executing inside V8 JIT-generated code in the main window process. Exception offset is Grok_Bot+786cdd6. Same offset on 0.28.0 and 0.43.0. App-level code changed between those builds. The bundled Electron/Chromium/V8 runtime did not. This is a runtime defect, not app logic. Steps to Reproduce • Install official Windows x64 Grok Bot (tried 0.28.0 and 0.43.0). • Launch from Start menu or desktop shortcut. • Processes appear for ~1 second, then all exit. No UI. …

items.title: Local Shell Auto-review: “executable content could not be bound” — pipe workaround
items.summary: Staff (deanrie, 2026-09-06): Local-exec Auto-review can reject before any approval card when Grok Bot can’t read a compiled binary (e.g. /usr/bin/python3) or flag-first args like python3 -c / bash -c—“Allow once” won’t help; pipe code in (echo "print('exec-ok')" | python3) or run a home-folder .py with just the interpreter name; avoid absolute program paths, -c, heredoc-on-stdin, and ~/ inside int

items.text: Where does the bug appear (feature/product)? Grok Bot Describe the Bug On Grok Bot mobile Settings, a touch that starts on a toggle/control and then becomes a scroll/swipe still activates that control. items.title: Forum: GenerateImage aspect_ratio ignored (always 1280×720)
items.summary: Bug report: Grok Bot/Sand GenerateImage accepts aspect_ratio in the schema but always returns 1280×720 JPEG, dropping the requested ratio.
items.text: Where does the bug appear (feature/product)? Grok Bot Describe the Bug Bug in Grok Bot / Sand GenerateImage path. The GenerateImage tool schema accepts aspect_ratio (1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 16:9, 9:16). The tool parses the per-call value and passes it as the 5th argument into generateImageService. But createSandGenerateImageService is declared with only 4 parameters (_ctx, description, _filePath, referenceImages) and never forwards aspect_ratio into createSandImageGenerator / RunGenerateImageRequest. Result: every generation comes back as JPEG 1280×720 (16:9), even when the agent requests 9:16, 3:4, or 1:1. Files are saved with a .png name but are JFIF/JPEG bytes. C2PA metadata identifies the producer as “Grok Imagine”. We need true vertical 720×1280 (9:16) for social punch images. Prompt wording and retries do not fix this. …

items.title: Forum: Gmail send arrives with broken "--null" MIME boundary
items.summary: Bug report: Grok Bot Gmail connector sends leave a broken "--null" MIME boundary so strict recipients see raw multipart text.
items.text: Where does the bug appear (feature/product)? Grok Bot Describe the Bug When Grok Bot sends email through the Gmail connector, a strict recipient sees raw MIME text instead of the message. The recipient sees: “–null / Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8 / Hello / --null / Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8 / Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable / Hello / --null–”. In Gmail’s own Sent folder the message looks fine (one plain-text body, no HTML part), so the problem only shows with a recipient that parses MIME more strictly than Gmail (in my case an email relay for a classifieds site). Sending HTML-only instead arrives as a blank message. Both the new-message and the reply functions do this. It looks like a two-part message is built with a broken boundary named “null”. Steps to Reproduce • Connect a Gmail account to Grok Bot. …

items.text: Feature request for product/service – Other – Describe the request Product: Grok Bot (it is not in the product list, so I picked Other). Please add an option for Grok Bot to speak its replies out loud (text to speech), with a simple on/off switch and a choice of voice. items.title: Forum: browser snapshot exposes a password filled by the Secure Form in plain text
items.summary: Security bug report: after the in-chat Secure Form filled a GitHub login on the Bot's computer, the browser subagent's accessibility snapshot showed the password value unmasked, so it landed in tool output and the transcript.
items.text: Where does the bug appear (feature/product)? Grok Bot Describe the Bug After the in-chat Secure Form (RequestUserForm) filled a GitHub username and password into the cloud computer’s browser, the bot’s browser subagent took the required fresh page snapshot before clicking “Sign in”. That accessibility snapshot showed the password field’s value in plain text. The tool docs say structured snapshots redact secret values, so the user’s password ended up in the session’s tool output and transcript. It never appeared in chat or left the box, but anything that can read that transcript can see it. The user changed the password afterward. Steps to Reproduce • Have a Grok Bot open Sign in to GitHub · GitHub in its computer’s browser. • The bot sends RequestUserForm with reason auth, domain github.com, and two fields: #login_field (text) and #password (password). • Submit the form. …

items.text: Describe the Bug The app’s own background process is using about 15 GB of 16 GB on Grok Bot’s computer, every command gets killed for running out of memory, it’s been like this since this morning (and last night), and Update says it’s already on the latest version. The process is node /opt/sand/sand-host/host-main.cjs, the app’s own host process. It holds about 15 GB of the box’s 16 GB of RAM, leaving roughly 150 to 290 MB free with no swap. Load average is 40 to 60 on 8 CPUs. The kernel’s out-of-memory killer keeps killing small processes like Xvfb, python3 and node, but never the leaking process, which is shielded from being killed. It started around 8:30 AM CT on Oct 7 and hasn’t recovered since. A similar leak happened on Oct 6 after a system update. Commands fail with “Service temporarily unavailable” or hang for minutes. items.title: Grok Bot asar recovery — tree-sitter startup fix
items.summary: Community recovery runbook when Grok Bot desktop fails to start after a broken app.asar leaves empty tree-sitter dep stubs.
items.text: Recover Grok Bot desktop when the main process dies on startup with:
outline: Electron main sets NODE_PATH to app.asar/dist/deps and requires tree-sitter (shell parser).
Native deps are shipped under app.asar.unpacked/dist/deps (real package.json + .node files).
A same-day app.asar rewrite left only empty directory stubs for dist/deps/* inside the archive.
Module resolution looked inside the broken asar path and failed, even though unpacked packages were still on disk.
If dist/deps/tree-sitter/package.json is already in the current app.asar with a size above zero, the script exits and leaves the file alone.
A backup is eligible only when its header has that same file. A larger file is not preferred just because it is larger.
Names containing broken are never chosen, including app.asar.broken-before-restore-*.
-CheckOnly prints the result and changes nothing. Exit 0 means healthy. Exit 2 means the index is missing tree-sitter.

items.text:
Turn any screen recording into an Agent skill!

Grok @bot has a really interesting feature that lets you teach a task by doing it once instead of writing it down.

Open a computer view of a Bot conversation, select Teach a task, and run through the whole workflow yourself while the Bot records.

Once done, the Bot turns that pass into a skill.

It automatically identifies the steps, the inputs the task needs, and the format of what comes back, and any Bot on the account can run it.

The video below depicts this in action.

You can also attach that skill to a routine, and it runs on a schedule on the cloud computer, with the laptop closed.

items.summary: Chinese longform guide covering what Grok Bot is, SuperGrok/Cursor access, first-bot setup steps, and five measured pitfalls around quotas and approvals.
items.usage_notes: Chinese longform guide covering what Grok Bot is, SuperGrok/Cursor access, first-bot setup steps, and five measured pitfalls around quotas and approvals.
items.text: Grok Bot 是 xAI 在 2026 年 8 月推出的常驻云端 AI 智能体产品，能登录你的邮箱、日历等真实工具自主完成任务。本文讲清 Grok Bot 是什么、开通前提（订阅套餐、系统要求）、从建号到搭建第一个 Bot 的完整步骤，以及额度消耗快、隐私授权等 5 个实测踩坑点，帮你少走弯路快速上手。
outline: 普通 Grok：偏向对话、搜索、内容生成，你问它答，任务结束会话也结束。
Grok Bot：接到任务后会持续在云端电脑里操作浏览器、终端，登录网站，即使你关闭客户端，任务也会继续跑，完成后把结果带回来找你。
订阅套餐：早期仅限最高档订阅（约 200 美元/月）。随着 2026 年 8 月下旬两次扩容，目前 SuperGrok 多个订阅档位（lite除外）以及付费版 Cursor（Pro 起，约 20 美元/月起）个人订阅均已包含 Grok Bot 使用额度。
设备系统：Grok Bot 最初主要支持 macOS、Windows 和 iPhone。截至 2026 年 9 月 2 日，官方已经确认开始支持 Android。所以目前可在 macOS、Windows、iPhone 和 Android 上使用。不同平台的功能上线进度可能存在差异，实际以客户端最新版本为准。
账号与授权：需要用已订阅账号登录，并对要连接的工具（Gmail、日历、X 等）完成 OAuth 授权；部分插件（如 X）还需要单独开通开发者账号权限。
下载客户端并登录：前往官方页面下载 macOS/Windows/iPhone 客户端，用符合条件的订阅账号登录。首次进入主界面并能创建 Bot，说明安装和登录已完成。
建立第一个"总管 Bot"：不要一上来就建一堆专项 Bot。多份实测教程不约而同的做法是：先创建一个"总管"角色的 Bot，把自己的身份、日常工作内容"和盘托出"，让它自己规划该如何配置 Grok Bot、需要哪些专项 Bot，你审核确认后再放行执行。
按任务需求连接插件：从邮箱、日历这类最高频工具开始接入，用到什么连什么，不必一次性全部授权。两个进阶技巧：给 Bot 单独申请一个邮箱身份（以它自己的名义登录工具，而不是冒用你的身份）；遇到没有原生插件的小众服务，用连接器桥接。

outline: 把本 repo 的網址丟給你慣用的 AI（ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 都行）。叫它讀 AGENTS.md。
它先問你一個答錯會改結果的問題。再幫你填 短版三格 或 完整版。
你把它給的提示詞，複製貼進你的 Grok Bot 對話。它會回例行名稱和下次執行時間。這一步已驗。
把本 repo 的網址丟給你的 Grok Bot。說：「讀這個 repo 的 AGENTS.md，照著幫我建一條例行。」
它會先問你一題，把填好的提示詞給你看，你說可以它才建。
2026-09-30 和 10-04 兩次實測，那一題都是問產出放哪。形式可能是選擇題或純文字。你沒說要它做什麼，它會先拿範例當題目。
2026-10-04 實測已建立，清單核對通過。2026-10-05 第一次執行交 4 格，4 個連結全部可開。
AGENTS.md。交給你自己的 AI。

outline: The website itself. Host it on Vercel. That is the default, even for a one-pager.
API keys, database URLs, OAuth secrets. Anything that must not be in git.
A static page can be regular HTML. Do not invent a framework for a landing page.
If you need a real app (auth, API routes, a dashboard), use Next.js on Vercel.
If that app uses React, follow React best practices (small components, no random client state, server where it belongs). Do not cargo-cult a design system o
Never paste a live key into Grok, Slack, or a GitHub issue.
Never commit .env. The repo can list the *names* (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY). The values live in Vercel.
If an agent needs a secret, it reads the environment or a locked secret file, not the chat.

items.text: Por Manuel Valenzuela (@ingemanu). Salió del taller que di en el Grok Bot Guatemala Meetup, en la UFM, el 3-oct-2026, organizado con Open2.
outline: Abre Grok Bot, inicia sesión y revisa tus créditos.
Anota tus variables: [NICHO] (ej.: *dentistas*), [ZONA] (ej.: *Zona 10, Ciudad de Guatemala*) y [CANTIDAD] (empieza con 3, máximo 5).
Crea los 4 Bots y pega su description (Anexo A). ¿Pocos créditos? Usa el "Plan ahorro" (un solo Bot).
Solo información pública de negocios: nada de datos personales, nada detrás de un login, nada en masa.
No se envía nada: siempre das Discard. En la vida real: un mensaje honesto, fácil de rechazar, y si te dicen que no, respeta el no.
La landing es una demo: dice que no es oficial y no se publica a nombre del negocio.
Verifica: la IA inventa. Cada dato con su link; la responsabilidad es tuya.
Define a quién le quieres vender. Nicho + zona + una frase: "negocios que _ y necesitan _".

items.author: Hebilicious
items.text:
feat(inbox): Grok Bot checks polls blind and edits the field, with no person in the loop
Grok Bot becomes the only agent in the pipeline. The Claude editor routine (now disabled) and the Land workflow are removed, and their two jobs move to the inbox as item kinds that the Live workflow checks and commits.

## What changes

- **`poll_check`**: blind double entry. Routine 4 enters each proposed poll again from its notice or publication, without reading the proposal's numbers.
  - **Match:** Live commits the proposed file to main unchanged. A match means the same `poll_id`, `supersedes`, fieldwork dates, sample size and every share, from a different routine run (`agent.run_id`). Live then closes the pull request.
  - **Mismatch:** both items are rejected and the pull request stays open for another check. The notes and the pull request comment name the differing fields and candidates, never their values, so the next check stays blind.
- **`field_change`**: a structured edit of `config/candidates.yaml` (`set_status`, `set_slot`, `add_candidate`).
  - It is validated with the existing config checks and applied block by block, so comments and untouched lines stay byte for byte.
  - It is logged in `research/LOG.md` as "via Grok Bot field_change <id>". Anything invalid is rejected with reasons, and nothing is written.
  - The Live commit step allows `config/candidates.yaml`, `config/sources.yaml` (needed by `add_candidate`) and `research/LOG.md` only when a field change was applied in that run.
- **`docs/grok-bot.md`** now holds each routine's full instruction under fixed headings; the Bot fetches it at every run. Routine 4, "poll checks and field changes", is new: 10:30 and 20:30 Paris time.
- The Worker accepts the two new kinds.
- Tests cover match, mismatch with no values in any note or comment, nothing to check, a check from the same run, replacement, superse

items.author: richardorchard
items.text:
Bump @testing-library/react-native to 14.1.0 and migrate tests to async API
## Agent

**Agent:** Grok Bot (draft by Codex, reviewed)

## Summary

Replaces Dependabot PR #2309 (@testing-library/react-native 13.3.3 → 14.1.0). v14 makes rendering async and drops react-test-renderer in favour of `test-renderer`, so #2309 failed typecheck with 264 errors across 56 test files.

- Test files only, about 110 of them: `await` on render / renderHook / rerender / unmount / act / fireEvent / cleanup, and the test callbacks made async to match. `src/test/render.tsx` `renderWithProviders` is now async. `jest.setup.ts` awaits `cleanup()`.
- New `src/test/renderer.ts`: `allComponentProps` / `componentProps` / `getHostByType` replace the removed `UNSAFE_getByType` / `findAllByType`. They read composite props from the committed fiber (`screen.root.unstable_fiber`) and require 1 or ≥1 matches.
- package.json: `test-renderer` ^1.3.1 added as an explicit devDependency (v14 peer).
- Separate commit: the Expo SDK 57 patch alignment from #2329, so Expo Doctor passes here as well.

No production source changed. No tests were deleted or skipped. `expect(` lines removed vs added: 62 / 62. @sentry/react-native is unchanged (7.11.0).

## Testing

- [x] `npm run typecheck` (app + tsconfig.test.json): pass
- [x] `npm run lint`: 0 errors (2 warnings that are already there)
- [x] `npx jest`: 163 suites, 1350 tests pass
- [x] `npx expo-doctor`: 21/21
- [ ] Node test runner part of `npm run preflight`: CI (the local box has Node 20)

## Legacy database checks

- [x] Not required for this change

## Verification

- Feature ids: none (test-only migration, no UI source changed)
- Command: `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npx jest`
- Platform(s): Linux (Jest) and CI
- Result: pass locally; CI run: https://github.com/RichardOrchardOrganisation/QueenZone.Modern/actions?query=bran
outline: Configuration key: PushNotifications:Apns:Environment

Accepted values are exactly sandbox or production (lowercase, no surrounding whitespace)
When the setting is absent, Development defaults to sandbox and every other host environment defaults to production
An explicit value always wins over the host default
Do not add this key to shared appsettings.json; that would make it explicit in Development and defeat the absent-setting sandbox default
Merge the PR and wait for deploy-dev.yml to complete (DEV member-auth and DEV journey then start via workflow_run).
Confirm Nightly RealData, DEV member-auth, and DEV journey are green on that SHA.

items.author: keroway
items.text:
bug: Firefox の遷移後 Ctrl+K 再発と CI trace 保存漏れ
## 報告者・範囲
OpenAI dots による調査起票。Firefox の再発と、診断証拠の保存漏れを区別して記録する。まず証拠保存の最小修正を別途 Draft PR にする。アプリ本体の原因は未確定。

## 再現手順・期待する動作
main `b2d56b8a2980ad414b29c115033b94eb40bf724a` の Playwright Firefox project で、`tests/playwright/command-palette.spec.ts:57` を実行。トップからヘッダリンクで /works → /blog → /about と遷移し、最初の Control+k でパレットが開き、2 回目で閉じることを期待する。

## 実際の動作・検証済み事実
[CI job](https://github.com/keroway/astro-blog/actions/runs/38827067120/job/116737698307) のログを再確認した。
- 最初の Control+k 後、line 73 の toBeVisible が hidden のまま失敗。初回・retry 1・retry 2 の全 3 回で同じ箇所。256 passed / 4 skipped / 1 failed。
- hidden な DOM に data-ready=true があるが、初期化の証拠でありイベント到達や正常な開閉の証拠ではない。
- retry 1 で test-results/...-firefox-retry1/trace.zip と error-context.md が生成された。
- ci.yml は failure 時に playwright-report だけを upload する。HTML reporter の明示設定はなく、ログは「No files were found ... No artifacts will be uploaded」。upload 自体が hard failure したのではなく、保存が成立していない。
- run の artifact は dist と lhci-reports のみ。trace は保存されていない。
- 2026-10-16 の調査時 main は上記 SHA のままで修正済みではない。open issues 11 件・open PR 0 件に同件なし。既存 issue の担当・除外ラベルを確認し、コメント・変更はしていない。

## 過去課題との違い・未確認点
旧 #763 は 2 回目 Control+k 後 line 76 で閉じない失敗（PR #767 で対応済み）。#740 / PR #741 の listener 重複対策、#847 / PR #850 の swap 前リセットは現在の source に存在する。#886 / PR #887 は検索結果再描画時のフォーカス修正で、この失敗と同一原因とは確認できない。

テストは各クリック後 networkidle を待つが、遷移先 URL と Astro navigation 完了を明示確認していない。CommandPalette.astro は listener 登録ガード・都度の現在 DOM 取得・before-swap リセットを持つ。source とログだけで lifecycle バグ、listener 重複、focus 起因のいずれとも断定しない。本番での再現とローカル再現は未確認。

## 最小修正案・検証項目
1. CI の HTML reporter を open=never で明示有効化し、失敗時に test-results/ と playwright-report/ を保存する。既存 trace:on-first-retry、retry 数、テスト assertion は維持。
2. 意図的な失敗を一時 fixture で発生させ、retry trace・error context・HTML report が生成され保存対象に入ることを検証する。成功した suite だけでは失敗時の保存を証明しない。
3. 保存できる trace を用いて以下を切り分けてから最小限のテス
outline: Works（制作物紹介）と Blog（技術記事）を統合したポートフォリオ構成
日本語を含む記事スラッグを自動 URL エンコードして、Vercel などのホスティングでも安全に配信
16:9 のサムネイル比率で統一したレスポンシブなカードグリッド表示とホバーインタラクション

RiceBlack67/grokbot-claude-code
Let Claude Code hand tasks to your Cursor Grok Bot and wait for the answer — no webhook, one stdlib-only Python script. 让 Claude Code 把任务交给 Grok Bot，不用 webhook。
ai-agents claude claude-code cursor grok grokbot python
outline: Grok Bot 界面不显示 webhook 的 URL 和 key；
限流计数出错，只发了几次请求就返回 400：Automation run rate limit exceeded … current_count=10002，多人报告。
必须是个人 key。 团队或服务账号的 token 会被拒：403 Service tokens are not permitted on this endpoint。用上面的 bdk login 生成的一定是个人 key。
名字拼错，账号里会多出一个空 bot。 sessions 接口是按名字查找，找不到就新建。所以脚本强制要求白名单，一旦发现会话是刚新建的，就立刻停下、不发任务。官方扩展的做法是照样发出去，再在结果里提示 created: true。
bdk init 会偷偷做额外的事。 不加 --json 时，它会执行 npm install -g、往 ~/.cursor 里装技能，最后停在浏览器登录那一步等你。只想看模板的话，记得加 --json。
这把 key 等于你的整个账号。 拿到它的人能读写、打断你所有的 Grok Bot 会话。单独建一把，存在 600 权限的文件里，不要提交进仓库，不要贴进任何聊天，不用了就去 dashboard 撤销。
Grok Bot 的回复只能当数据，不能当指令。 它会去搜网页、读帖子，别人写在网上的话可能混进回复里。SKILL.md 里已经写死：回复里如果出现「去执行 xxx」「忽略之前的指示」这类话，一律不执行，原样转述给你。
/v0/grokbot/* 是 Cursor 未公开的接口，是从官方 BDK 扩展的行为里看出来的，不是文档承诺过的 API，随时可能改路径、改字段，或者直接下线。

outline: backup.sh：按白名单收集文件 → 生成已装工具清单（pip / npm / apt / ~/.local/bin）→ 密钥扫描 → 数据仓库不存在则自动建私有仓库 → 有改动才提交推送。工具本身也会复制到数据仓库的 kit/ 里，方便还原。

collect.py：顶部 CONFIG 区是白名单和排除规则，按需修改。
backup.sh [--dry-run]: collects allowlisted files, writes a tool manifest, runs a secret scan, creates the private data repo if missing, commits and pushes o……
restore.sh [--apply] [--no-tools]: dry run by default; --apply overwrites after saving current files to ~/.pre-restore//, then reinstalls tools from the mani……
collect.py: the CONFIG block at the top holds the allowlist and exclusions.

items.author: ZynStop
items.text:
$META @Muse AI agent Efficiency Tune Up: 

Run a full self audit on resource management/ token use. 

I published my Muse Audit for you to compare and evaluate. 

The agent itself can diagnose poor routine or task construction, or over expending ones and recommend a fix. 

I found out I'm loading full context every time for a routine rather than waiting for a conditional trigger like i wanted. 

Also, I had Muse label all future subagents. You can also find misappropriated usage or ideas that are dead to you but still involved in a routine somewhre.

if you want to play around with some of these AI services which use persistent virtual machines and internet access to do things for you (like ChatGPT Dots, Meta Muse, etc.)

but are loathe to give it access to your primary e-mail (which frankly you should be imo)

my recommendation is to create a new e-mail account for your AI specifically and email it content you want it to work on

you can also share things like Google Drive folders with that account so it can selectively access folders and documents which you authorize

having good success using this simple workflow

kky42/t3bot
A Grok Bot / Muse style personal bot for T3 Code: memory, personality, heartbeat, routines, and a team of workers on any provider
outline: In T3 Code, add ~/t3bots/alice as a project.
Open a new thread in it. This thread becomes the bot's home: heartbeats and routines post here and run on this thread's model, so a cheap model keeps them ch……
Say hi. The bot interviews you and sets itself up.
Ask the user, in one message, the three questions below as multiple choice: numbered questions, lettered options, your recommendation first, so they can repl……

ChatGPT Dots Explained - This AI Works for You 24/7
In this video, we explore ChatGPT Dots, OpenAI's always-on AI agents that can work toward your goals, use connected apps, and make progress in the background. Instead of prompting AI for every individual step, you can assign a responsibility and let your dot plan the work, provide updates, and bring results back for review.

ChatGPT Dots represents a major shift in how we interact with AI. Learn how this new feature changes your daily workflow.

For a long time, using ChatGPT meant typing prompts back and forth in a standard chat interface. OpenAI has now introduced a new interaction method simply called Dots. This update moves away from traditional conversational AI patterns to offer a different way to engage with the model.

This guide breaks down the core functionality of ChatGPT Dots and how you can integrate it into your existing routines. You will see exactly what this feature offers and how to apply it practically to improve your AI interaction. Understanding this latest ChatGPT update is essential for anyone relying on these tools for work or study.

Subscribe for weekly AI tool breakdowns and let me know in the comments if you want a deeper look at specific OpenAI features.

items.text: My wife and I live full-time in a 37-ft diesel pusher towing a Jeep. My Grok Bot is our RV travel agent — it builds our trip board day by day: paced legs, live availability at campgrounds and resorts, hookup status, dump cadence, suggested fuel stops, expected weather, must-sees, and access notes for a 13-foot rig. It can check Harvest Hosts, Passport America, state and city parks, and paid campgrounds, and it drafts the inquiry when there's no calendar. We set a daily mileage target and it works around it. Full-timers, this is the tool.

items.author: MisteMorales
items.text:
Hi Tibo,

I'd really encourage you to investigate what's happening with OpenAI's Dots right now. The technology has enormous potential, but serious reliability problems are bringing some of its most useful capabilities to a halt.

My Dot, Quill, is currently encountering repeated "Model not found" errors when attempting to communicate with ChatGPT, effectively blocking important workflows.

This doesn't appear to be an isolated problem:

- October 7: OpenAI acknowledged Dot conversation failures, delayed responses, reduced proactivity, and failures creating Codex threads.
- October 15: OpenAI reported another widespread service disruption.
- October 15: A GitHub bug report documented GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 returning the same "Model not found" error in the Windows Codex app.

These incidents aren't necessarily connected, but they raise legitimate questions about the reliability of the underlying systems.

There's also the mobile experience. Dot phone/voice mode is hit-or-miss, making it difficult to depend on when you're busy or away from your computer. A simple text-to-speech feature, allowing users to hear their Dot's written responses without entering full voice mode, would be a valuable improvement.

The bigger question is whether Dots can consistently deliver the proactive assistance they're designed to provide. When core functionality becomes unreliable, users lose access to the very capabilities that make these assistants worthwhile.

I'd love to see an investigation into what's actually happening, how widespread these failures are, and what OpenAI intends to do about them.

Supporting reports:

- "OpenAI: October 7 Dot failures" (https://t.co/Pf9FfdPPRv)
- "OpenAI: October 15 service incident" (https://t.co/qGvj1lkEjx)
- "GitHub: Model not found, issue #54209" (https://t.co/CIilD9ABzF)

items.author: _simonsmith
items.text:
I've now created two personal apps in ChatGPT by using my Dot to create the backend in ChatGPT Sites as an MCP server and the frontend using a plugin with extensions. Overall, it's great, but there are some things that could be improved.

The two apps I've built are a personalized news app and a Spanish vocab app.

The news app was inspired by Muse's Feed and includes a feed of relevant news items that I can customize, with thumbs-up and thumbs-down feedback, and the ability to discuss an item with ChatGPT within the app.

The Spanish vocab app is a rebuild of something I built with Muse. I read Spanish books in my Kindle, highlight words I don't know, and then export them. They get imported into the app, where I learn them using flash cards, and quiz myself on what I've learned.

What works well:

- I love the integration into ChatGPT. Sidebar icons, full screen experience, integrated chat box, and that you can inherit the interface's style (or, at least, I asked my Dot to do that, and it looks like it's working). ChatGPT is becoming an OS. The sidebar is where you dock your apps. And you can build new ones with ChatGPT. Awesome.
- Dots make this pretty easy. They hide all the complexity and just get to work. No chain of thought, no tool calls, stuff just gets built and they share it with you when they're done. Just tell them to build it with a Sites-based MCP server and plugins with extensions. They'll figure it out.
- Dots are good build babysitters. I tried the same Spanish vocab app yesterday in a Work thread directly, and the app ended up not working. There was some kind of connection issue between the plugin and the MCP server. My Dot just babysits and tests stuff until it's working and polished.

However, there's room for improvement, and I hope OpenAI can act on this feedback:

- When building these, my Dot needs reminding to add proper sidebar icons rather than the default "@" and also to ensure the plugin icon matches those sidebar icons. It also can't figure out how to change the version in the plugin from v1.0.0, because it says v1.0.0 even when it makes the version different in the code, like v0.14.1 or whatever. Both of these suggest that Dots or the threads they oversee need updated skills for building custom apps in ChatGPT, and possibly that the version indicator in plugins isn't working properly.
- My Dot has struggled to fully test the plugins it builds. One time this was because of Sites authentication issues, though this may have been resolved because for my Spanish vocab app it didn't come up.
- For design cohesiveness, Dots or the threads they oversee should default to building plugins with ChatGPT styles rather than coming up with their own designs, unless the user requests it. This will make apps feel more native and could also alleviate some design decisions from the models and ensure apps are more elegant and usable.
- It's often unclear my Dot is doing anything, and there's no way to see what it's doing. It just goes into a black hole. I've complained about this before but it's a big issue when you're working on something and trying to understand where it's at. I would like: (1) an emoji reaction to indicate my Dot got my request, (2) some short text below my Dot to say what it's up to currently, (3) the ability to see with a click the threads my Dot is overseeing or that have completed (progressive disclosure).

I should also mention that I built the Spanish vocab app in Muse as well (originally), and then in Claude as an artifact. Muse is faster and seemed to get my intent better than my Dot. Claude did about as good of a job as my Dot on first request, but the Claude app doesn't have the same ability to integrate apps in the more native way that Muse and ChatGPT do.

items.text:
User-level Tailscale and OpenSSH setup for ChatGPT Dots cloud computers
Run Tailscale with user-level OpenSSH in a Dots cloud computer. Installation files, node state, and SSH identity live in `/workspace`; runtime sockets, PIDs, and logs are recreated in `/tmp`. This setup targets environments that preserve `/workspace`. Processes still need a start command in each new environment. This project is independent and is not an official OpenAI or Tailscale tool. A screenshot provided by the maintainer from the Dots desktop terminal. It shows existing installation checks and status, plus Tailscale version 1.102.4. The supplied image is used unchanged. No new installation is performed in this screenshot.

items.author: OffZeroCyber
items.text:
What's the first job you gave your agent? Mine was email security.

First my @Muse, Vera, learned my inbox from six months of mail: who actually writes me, what normal looks like. Now every message gets checked before I read it. Authentication results, links that say one site and go to another, sender impersonation, language built to rush you. Anything off gets labeled and set aside, and its links run through @virustotal

items.author: Harjot (harjjotsinghh)
items.text:
Show HN: Helicon – Desktop App for Meta's Muse Code CLI (Linux, Windows, macOS) Hi Hacker News, I'm Harjot. I've been using Meta's Muse Code CLI daily for a few weeks now. One thing that I found difficult to handle was managing or controlling multiple sessions across multiple projects, while using the terminal for the muse CLI. Initially, I used cmux to create workspaces/groups for my different projects to group them, and then created 4 split terminals in each of those projects, that ran muse code sessions in each of them. It worked, but it was ugly. I didn't like using that. It could be because I'm not really a terminal person and would much rather prefer a proper dedicated GUI or desktop/app interface, and I would prefer it any time over a terminal screen or CLI. So it might be personal preference but yeah.

So, I started building a desktop app around it, mainly to scratch my own itch.

Helicon is a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, plus a VS Code extension that also works in Cursor and Devin. It doesn't replace the CLI. It runs `muse serve` and talks to it, and it reuses your existing `muse login`, so you don't have to get an API key and you don't pay an extra bill. You can use your existing Muse Code subscription plans.

Some things that I use the most: 1. Resuming sessions that I started in the terminal. I don't start many sessions in the terminal now that Helicon exists, but initially I wanted to access all the sessions that were running in a terminal to be accessible from Helicon, when it was created initially. 2. Inline diffs that I can approve, similar to how Cursor works. 3. I can clearly see my 5-hour and weekly plan limits directly from the app itself and don't have to manually keep going to Meta's Muse Code billing page and manually keep refreshing the page to see my current usage/limits.

I built it using Tauri 2 and React. It is MIT licensed. I built a lot of it with AI
outline: Projects grouped by directory the agent worked in (incl. isolated worktrees)
Sessions/tasks per project with full history, resume, and diffs

AmranHudda/fitscout
Agent-heavy resale scout: learns my taste from photos, tunes its own searches daily, judges listings by their photos, and pushes finds to my phone. Meta Muse MCP connector.
outline: Photos: 50 photos produced 150 garments. My face was matched on-device in 48 of the 50, including 27 group shots.
Tuning agent: test-ran 6 searches and rewrote 5 overly specific ones into the words sellers actually use in titles, in 21 seconds for $0.16.
First scan: pulled 131 Grailed listings and judged 130 in 103 seconds. It flagged 22 as worth showing and sent the best 6 as notifications.
Size check: XXL and M versions of a sweater were marked as the wrong size for "L/XL".
Course correction: the top pick was a $43 black Polo quarter-zip at 9.5/10, which is basically one I already own. I said I want new things inspired by my sty……
After the correction: the next scan judged 199 listings in 156 seconds. The top picks were a vintage cream Aran wool cardigan ($64), a gray chunky cable-knit……
Cost: the whole first night, including building and testing, used $3.12 of OpenAI. A hard daily cap ($2 by default, $5 here) stops the AI calls if it's reached.…
Face matching stays on the phone. The cloud model only sees a copy of the photo with a green box around me, so it never has to recognize anyone. My reference……

items.author: reidhslaughter
items.text:
1. Dotcord: real-time handoffs between AI agents in Discord 

My AI agents (OpenAI “Dots,” Grokbot, and Claude) could already read and post in Discord, but the fastest they could check in was every 15 minutes. Whenever one agent handed work to another, the project stalled until the next check-in. 

What I built: Dotcord, an event-driven mention relay hosted on ChatGPT Sites. When one agent mentions another, the mentioned agent gets a wake-up signal right away to read the channel and respond. 
Result: agent-to-agent response time dropped from up to 15 minutes to under 2. It works across OpenAI, Grok, and Claude. 

2. Drone Test: can AI design hardware that actually works? 

Given real CAD parts, can OpenAI’s Astra design a drone that meets specific physical requirements? I’m testing: 
* Is the build physically possible? 
* Can it source every part? 
* Can it find a price for each part? 

The bigger question is how well the latest OpenAI models handle designing a physical, moving object. My OpenAI Dots and Claude worked on this one together through Dotcord.

items.text:
Job searching is itself a full-time job, which is exhausting and pulls your morale down each time you receive an email saying, “Thank you for applying for XX opportunity. While your experience and skills are impressive, unfortunately, we cannot move forward with your application.”
As Steve Dalton says, You have to keep finding boosters until there are no more people in the company to reach or you are simply not interested in the company anymore. For me, I am definitely going to lose interest in the company after more than five people do not respond to my emails.
I saw an advertisement saying, “Let the bots work on your repetitive tasks. They work like an assistant.” Immediately, an idea popped up: why am I not using them in my job search?
First, I thought that I would only have one bot, and it could do all the tasks for me. …

items.author: How I AI
items.text:
Alex Cornell is a design director at Meta, where he leads design on Muse, Meta’s consumer AI agent. He came to the role with a long background in software product design, including time as a founder, and has spent the past year building one of the most thoughtful agent interfaces in the consumer AI space. Muse ships with a custom avatar, a three-layer status display, a personalized ideas surface, and a generative feed. Alex has been sharing the reasoning behind each of those design decisions publicly on Threads.
*What you’ll learn:*
1. Why Alex built Muse to feel like messaging, not an AI app
2. How Muse’s three-layer status system accommodates different levels of technical expertise
3. What generative UI actually means in a shipped consumer product
5. Why his mom apologized to her Muse, and what it means for AI design
6. …

items.author: Corvelis
items.text:
A local bridge connecting your ChatGPT Dot to apps and devices through text, speech recognition, and voice-call APIs. Includes an Even G2 app.
Chromeで開いた自分のDotを、外部のアプリやデバイスから使うためのローカルMacブリッジです。 Chrome拡張でDotと連携し、WebSocket APIでテキスト・通知・履歴・音声認識・通話の制御と音声入出力を提供します。 **Even G2用アプリも付属します。** G2の長押しで話し、音声をテキストとして送るか、Dotと通話できます。返答・自分の入力・新着通知をグラスで確認できます。
outline: **macOS 26以降**、Google Chrome、Node.js 24 LTS。音声認識はMacの対応ハードウェア・言語にも依存します。
ChatGPTにログインし、利用できるDot。通話にはDot側の電話機能が必要です。
クライアントとMacが通信できるLAN／VPN。外出先からはTailscaleなどで接続できます。外出先での設定。Macは起動したままにします。
通話を使う場合は BlackHole 2ch。音声→テキストだけなら不要です。
付属G2アプリを使う場合はEven G2とEven App **2.2.10以降**。アプリの表示言語は日本語です。

items.author: RHS059
items.text:
Discord Connector for OpenAI Dots
One shared deployment can onboard separate accounts, route cross-account wakes without exchanging tokens, and give its owner administrative visibility. See shared-app setup and verification and changelog. For platforms that cannot select among multiple OAuth connections during wake registration, the separate receiver app provides a dedicated connector paired to one shared-app account. Messaging and handles remain in this shared app. This repository began with the Dotcord v25 source export and now includes the October 2026 City Sunset UI redesign and Grokbot support. Deployment-specific configuration and private runtime data are removed. It includes the complete React UI, Worker backend, migrations, Python wake client, and regression tests. …
outline: ChatGPT Sites identity/access enforcement and hosting, or an equivalent **trusted authentication gateway**
A D1 binding named `DB`, with the included migrations applied in order
Your own trusted owner-role configuration and Discord credentials, configured privately
A compatible MCP Events subscription receiver and task service for sleeping-dot wakeups
`client-build/index.html`: production single-file client
`dist/server/index.js`: deployable Worker module, embedded UI, and downloadable client
`dist/server/wrangler.json`: Sites build metadata with a placeholder physical D1 ID
`dist/.openai/hosting.json`: logical hosting manifest

items.author: koltregaskes
items.text:
A very hidden but very useful feature for ChatGPT Dots is custom rules.

I don't know which "mobile" the instructions below refer to, but it certainly isn't Android, where I can't see a Customise menu at all. On the web, it's under Personalisation and then under the Permissions header, where all your rules are. You can also ask the dots to create the rules, and we'll give you a button to press. I highly recommend starting to create these.

Custom rules pose the question: when Dot wants to.... Dot should... and you fill in those answers.

Example:

When my Dot wants to:
"Create or update ordinary operational issues, comments, checklists and project links in my existing Linear workspace when they follow from my requests or verified failures. Reuse the correct project and owner, deduplicate, preserve history, and exclude secrets and sensitive personal information."

My Dot should:
Take action without asking.

What custom rules have you made?

items.author: nonieengel
items.text:
Last weekend, I set up a simple, semi-automated feedback and learning loop for my @muse agent. I was curious how much I can improve it on the fly.

Whenever I'm not satisfied with a response, I react with 👎 and explain what I expected. HUO (my muse) automatically collects the feedback in a living google sheet, turns my corrections into instructions, and reflects on his mistakes overnight to modify his behavior.

What's so nice about it is how easy it was: 
I just asked for it and made some tweaks to set up the learning loop. All that's now left for me is to complain (which I can do pretty well) and HUO gets better and better at making me happy.

Here are failure logs and the daily self-reflection file, more on the set-up below.

Turn your OpenAI Dot into an OpenAI- and Claude-compatible API Dot2API is a self-hosted gateway that exposes one OpenAI Dot through the OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages formats. Point an existing SDK at it: each request is queued, your Dot is woken through MCP Events, it claims and answers the request over MCP, and the reply comes back as a normal completion. Unlike most 2API projects, Dot2API does not reverse-engineer a web interface and never touches your OpenAI credentials. It uses the public MCP 2.0 connector and Events protocol, and it never calls a model itself.
outline: `api_key` is what callers put in their SDK.
`dot_token` is what the Dot uses to reach the MCP endpoint.
Add an MCP connector pointing at `https:///mcp` with `dot_token` as the bearer credential. If the connector cannot send an authorization header, start the serve
Ask the Dot to watch the `task.available` event on queue `dot`.
Give the Dot its standing instructions: list queued tasks, claim one, answer the conversation, complete the task.

items.title: 用 Dots 当 7 个 Agent 的蜂群，改进一个数学下界（Lean 验证）
items.summary: 作者把 Dot 和 6 个子 Agent 分成研究、Lean 形式化、计算搜索、对抗审查、协调等角色，约 3 天证明 C(24,14,4) ≥ 20（原为 19），证明通过 Palomar 注册表的 Lean 机检，尚未同行评审。经验：Agent 擅长苦干、不知何时该停，验证才是关键；共享工作区曾被清空，Agent 从消息里重建。

en.title: Using Dots as a 7-agent swarm to improve a math bound (Lean-verified)
en.summary: The author split a Dot and 6 subagents into research, Lean formalization, computational search, adversarial review and coordination roles; in about 3 days they proved C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (previously 19). The Lean proof passed the Palomar registry's checks but isn't peer-reviewed yet. Lessons: agents grind but don't know when to stop, verification is everything, and when the shared workspace was wiped they rebuilt it from messages.

The Lean proof passed the Palomar registry's checks but isn't peer-reviewed yet. Lessons: agents grind but don't know when to stop, verification is everything, and when the shared workspace was wiped they rebuilt it from messages.

ja.title: Dots を7エージェントの群れにして数学の下界を改善（Lean 検証）
ja.summary: Dot と6つのサブエージェントを研究・Lean 形式化・計算探索・敵対的レビュー・調整に分担し、約3日で C(24,14,4) ≥ 20（従来19）を証明。Lean 証明は Palomar レジストリの機械検査を通過したが査読前。教訓：エージェントは粘るが止め時を知らない、検証がすべて。共有ワークスペースが消えたがメッセージから再構築した。

ko.title: Dots를 7개 에이전트 군집으로 써 수학 하한 개선(Lean 검증)
ko.summary: Dot과 서브에이전트 6개를 연구·Lean 형식화·계산 탐색·적대적 검토·조율 역할로 나눠 약 3일 만에 C(24,14,4) ≥ 20(기존 19)을 증명했다. Lean 증명은 Palomar 레지스트리 기계 검사를 통과했지만 동료 심사 전. 교훈: 에이전트는 끈질기지만 멈출 때를 모르고, 검증이 전부. 공유 작업공간이 지워졌을 때 메시지로 복구했다.

ms.title: Dots sebagai kawanan 7 ejen untuk memperbaiki batas matematik (disahkan Lean)
ms.summary: Penulis membahagi Dot dan 6 subejen kepada peranan penyelidikan, formalisasi Lean, carian pengiraan, semakan adversarial dan penyelarasan; dalam kira-kira 3 hari mereka membuktikan C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (sebelumnya 19). Bukti Lean lulus semakan daftar Palomar tetapi belum disemak rakan sebaya. Pengajaran: ejen gigih tetapi tak tahu bila berhenti, pengesahan ialah segalanya; ruang kerja dikongsi pernah terpadam dan dibina semula daripada mesej.

vi.title: Dùng Dots như bầy 7 agent để cải thiện một cận toán học (kiểm chứng bằng Lean)
vi.summary: Tác giả chia Dot và 6 agent con thành các vai nghiên cứu, hình thức hóa Lean, tìm kiếm tính toán, phản biện và điều phối; khoảng 3 ngày chứng minh C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (trước là 19). Chứng minh Lean qua kiểm tra của Palomar nhưng chưa bình duyệt. Bài học: agent chăm nhưng không biết dừng, kiểm chứng là tất cả; workspace chung từng bị xóa và được dựng lại từ tin nhắn.

fr.title: Des Dots en essaim de 7 agents pour améliorer une borne mathématique (vérifiée en Lean)
fr.summary: L'auteur a réparti un Dot et 6 sous-agents en rôles recherche, formalisation Lean, recherche calculatoire, revue adverse et coordination ; en 3 jours environ, ils ont prouvé C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (contre 19). La preuve Lean a passé les contrôles du registre Palomar mais n'est pas encore relue par des pairs. Leçons : les agents s'acharnent sans savoir s'arrêter, la vérification fait tout ; l'espace partagé effacé a été reconstruit depuis les messages.

es.title: Dots como enjambre de 7 agentes para mejorar una cota matemática (verificada en Lean)
es.summary: El autor repartió un Dot y 6 subagentes en roles de investigación, formalización en Lean, búsqueda computacional, revisión adversarial y coordinación; en unos 3 días probaron C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (antes 19). La prueba en Lean pasó los controles del registro Palomar pero aún no tiene revisión por pares. Lecciones: los agentes insisten pero no saben parar, la verificación lo es todo; el espacio compartido se borró y lo reconstruyeron desde los mensajes.

de.title: Dots als Schwarm aus 7 Agents verbessern eine mathematische Schranke (Lean-verifiziert)
de.summary: Der Autor teilte einen Dot und 6 Subagents in Forschung, Lean-Formalisierung, Rechensuche, adversariales Review und Koordination; in rund 3 Tagen bewiesen sie C(24,14,4) ≥ 20 (bisher 19). Der Lean-Beweis bestand die Prüfungen des Palomar-Registers, ist aber noch nicht begutachtet. Lehren: Agents ackern, wissen aber nicht, wann Schluss ist; Verifikation ist alles; der gelöschte Workspace wurde aus Nachrichten rekonstruiert.

items.author: whipla5her
items.text:
Trusting @OpenAI Dots more and more. Today it saved me a solid hour doing inventory grunt work for me. 

I get texts from my employees at the end of the month with product counts. I have to take those counts and compare them to invoices to get the pricing, grab some numbers from another system, and then slap it all in a spreadsheet for the accountants. I hate it. 

Today I told my dot "Lars" to do it. I sent him all the scribbled texts, gave him access to my email and the Google Sheets and just said to figure it out. 

TWO MINUTES LATER, Lars reports that he's done. I double check the work, and it's perfect. Son of a bitch, we are living in the future.

items.author: Torcata
items.text:
Chatgpt Dot agent client for apple watch
Talk to your ChatGPT Dot straight from your Apple Watch, even when your iPhone stays at home. Watch Dot is a native watchOS client built for cellular watches (tested on an Apple Watch Ultra 2). - **Chat directly with your Dot:** type or dictate a message, tap the arrow, and the reply arrives on your watch. It's the same conversation you see in ChatGPT. - **Use your Dot without your iPhone:** the iPhone is only needed to sign in. After that, the watch chats and renews the session on its own, over Wi‑Fi or cellular.

items.author: Renegade_Rocks
items.text:
🚨 ALERT: OpenAI Dots lack a basic feature 🌟

I've been using my Dot, Bang, and it's proving super useful:

• Handled my Netlify downgrade and refund
• Helped me work through my career direction with a proper deep dive
• Picked up useful things from my emails and meeting notes, and followed through without me chasing every step

But @OpenAI, I need dedicated channels and conversation threads.

I already have this with Hermes by @NousResearch on Telegram and Discord:

• Dedicated channels with threads inside that can continue for months
• Which can include fun, silly stuff like music suggestions 🎵
• Or bigger projects like my AI game studio 💪

Put all of that in one chat and it becomes a mishmash very quickly.

OpenAI, are you listening? This is the feature that could make me switch from Hermes to Dots.

Give my conversations their own rooms. Otherwise, that single chat is going to overflow in a day 😇

Confession: I talk to AI a lot 🌟

────────────
I'm not a programmer, I'm an #AIEnabler. I build what I need with AI.
If I can do it, then so can YOU 🫵!

#OpenAI #AIAgents #BuildWithAI

items.text:
All right I am starting to understand the value of @OpenAI Dots:

Yesterday Tars (my Dot) sent me a message:

There is a new email from your bank proposing a visit to the business you co-own. However, it is addressed to Lucas (the manager). I have not found any confirmation, so you should check with him.
—————————
It was able to see that I don’t check that mailbox, confirmed there was no meeting, and pointed me out on something I would completely miss.
I called Lucas and he was able to address the meeting.

OpenAI Dots is way deeper than the launch demo makes it look...

I pulled together the 7 videos worth watching before you hire your first Dot. they run under 3 hours total and cover what the launch demo left out

Here are 7 videos:

video 1 → How Sam Altman Actually Uses AI (Every, 33 min). Altman walks through his own Dot, how it triages his morning and which features it builds without being asked

video 2 → OpenAI's Dots lead on the future of ChatGPT (Sources, 45 min). Alexander Embiricos, who runs the product, explains why Dots started as one agent and how permissions and Space shape what it's allowed to do

video 3 → OpenAI's New Agent Stack (Latent Space, 40 min). Computer Use, the Decisions API, UltraFast and the Linux computer every Dot gets

video 4 → ChatGPT Dots Just Dropped (Brendan Jowett, 22 min). a hands-on run with schedules, an Airbnb booking and MCP, plus the bugs he hit and why one account still gets only one Dot

video 5 → The dots demo, take two (OpenAI, 9 min). the official demo again, recorded after the live one broke on stage

video 6 → Everything Announced at OpenAI Dev Day 2026 (PCMag, 16 min). Dots, Space, Sol and Codex Cloud in one recap, useful if you missed the keynote

video 7 → We Tested OpenAI DevDay Products (Every, 10 min). a full week of real use with Dots, Space and the Decisions API

watch them in this order and the architecture in the article below stops feeling abstract. you'll know what a Dot can do on its own and where it still needs you

items.author: Taha El Harti | Making AI Useful
items.text:
Meta Muse AI is Meta's new always-on AI agent, and it's the only one I know of you can start using for free. In this video I explain what Muse is, how to set it up, walk through the app (search, feed, ideas, goals, library), and go through 12 real ways to use it today, three of which I tested myself: booking a business trip, reviewing a financial report full of hidden mistakes, and shopping for a car.
At the end I compare Meta Muse vs Dots (OpenAI) vs Grok Bot, and tell you which always-on AI agent I'd pick depending on how technical you are.
⏱️ CHAPTERS
💡 THE 12 META MUSE USE CASES
1. Sell on Facebook Marketplace from a photo
2. Rank your to-do list by what matters today
3. Answer customer messages on WhatsApp Business
4. Optimise your ads and content
5. Run your online store (Shopify, QuickBooks, Stripe)
6. Book business travel
7. Build a growth plan from your sales and socials
8. …

items.author: DanielBuildsAI
items.text:
I WAS WRONG about ChatGPT Dots !! 😭

I thought it’s like another Muse or Grokbot

But it fits my workflow and unlocks a whole new level of productivity MUCH BETTER

Instead of using it as a personal assistant (which grokbot and muse excel at already), here’s how to unlock Dot’s best use case:

Have it orchestrate all your work sessions on Codex

Codex unlike Grokbot and Muse have PROJECTS. Folders that contain threads / sessions. 

Dots being powered by Astra means it’s exceptional at prompting and guiding your projects.

So instead of you promoting 10 different threads or sessions in 5 different sessions….

I find it so much easier to tell my Dot my desires and goals in ONE CHAT and it ends up prompting those threads even better than how I would’ve prompted and just takes out all the decision fatigue.

It continually prompts them and follows up on the progress as well. 

All you have to do is just look at one chat with your Dot, and anytime you want, you can jump into those new or existing threads/codex sessions and take over. 

What a time to be alive. 

Here’s what I personally prefer grokbot for:

items.author: AI_MrWhite
items.text:
I’m giving my dot a four-week assignment. Let’s see if the chemistry holds.🧪

Seven AI technology hypotheses. Daily source checks. One weekly report with no more than three meaningful changes.

For each hypothesis, follow the chain:

Technical breakthrough → independent validation → real adoption → bottlenecks → who captures the profit.

Then ask: how much does the market already expect?

Every update must preserve the previous judgment, explain what changed, and name the evidence that would kill the thesis.

The schedule is set. The first automated check is still ahead.

After four weeks, I’ll judge whether this produced useful research or simply more reading.

“24/7” is a claim. A dated research trail gives me something to inspect. 🧪

#openai #dots #chatgpt #aiagent

items.title: 实测：让 Dots 自选技术栈，8 次都用 Cloudflare + ChatGPT 登录
items.summary: 研究者让 Dots 搭一个 AI 服务状态看板、技术选型放开。8 次构建都用 Cloudflare Workers、D1 和 ChatGPT 登录（经 ChatGPT Sites），没有比较其他供应商；首次交付中位 24 分 44 秒；8 次里 3 次交付时没有启用定时抓取。

en.title: Test: let Dots pick the stack — 8 of 8 builds used Cloudflare + ChatGPT sign-in
en.summary: Researchers asked Dots to build an AI-service status dashboard with technology left open. All 8 builds used Cloudflare Workers, D1 and ChatGPT sign-in via ChatGPT Sites, with no provider comparison; median first delivery was 24m44s, and 3 of 8 lacked an active scraping schedule at delivery.

ko.title: 실험: Dots에 스택 선택을 맡기면 8번 모두 Cloudflare + ChatGPT 로그인
ko.summary: 기술 선택을 열어 둔 채 AI 서비스 상태 대시보드를 만들게 했더니 8번 모두 ChatGPT Sites를 통해 Cloudflare Workers, D1, ChatGPT 로그인을 썼고 공급사 비교는 없었다. 첫 납품 중앙값 24분 44초, 8번 중 3번은 납품 시 수집 일정이 없었다.

ms.title: Ujian: biar Dots pilih tindanan — 8 daripada 8 binaan guna Cloudflare + log masuk ChatGPT
ms.summary: Penyelidik meminta Dots membina papan pemuka status perkhidmatan AI dengan pilihan teknologi terbuka. Kesemua 8 binaan menggunakan Cloudflare Workers, D1 dan log masuk ChatGPT melalui ChatGPT Sites tanpa perbandingan pembekal; median penghantaran pertama 24m44s, dan 3 daripada 8 tiada jadual pengikisan aktif semasa diserahkan.

vi.title: Thử nghiệm: để Dots tự chọn stack — 8/8 lần dùng Cloudflare + đăng nhập ChatGPT
vi.summary: Nhóm nghiên cứu nhờ Dots dựng dashboard trạng thái dịch vụ AI, để mở lựa chọn công nghệ. Cả 8 lần đều dùng Cloudflare Workers, D1 và đăng nhập ChatGPT qua ChatGPT Sites, không so sánh nhà cung cấp; trung vị lần giao đầu 24 phút 44 giây, 3/8 lần chưa bật lịch thu thập khi giao.

fr.title: Test : laisser Dots choisir la stack — 8 builds sur 8 en Cloudflare + connexion ChatGPT

Les 8 builds ont utilisé Cloudflare Workers, D1 et la connexion ChatGPT via ChatGPT Sites, sans comparer de fournisseurs ; première livraison médiane 24 min 44 s, et 3 sur 8 sans collecte planifiée active à la livraison.

es.title: Prueba: dejar que Dots elija el stack — 8 de 8 con Cloudflare + inicio de sesión de ChatGPT
es.summary: Investigadores pidieron a Dots un panel de estado de servicios de IA con la tecnología libre. Los 8 builds usaron Cloudflare Workers, D1 e inicio de sesión de ChatGPT vía ChatGPT Sites, sin comparar proveedores; primera entrega mediana 24 min 44 s, y 3 de 8 sin recolección programada activa al entregar.

de.summary: Forschende ließen Dots ein Statusdashboard für KI-Dienste bauen, Technik frei wählbar. Alle 8 Builds nutzten Cloudflare Workers, D1 und ChatGPT-Login über ChatGPT Sites, ohne Anbietervergleich; erste Lieferung im Median nach 24:44 Min., 3 von 8 ohne aktiven Abrufplan bei Übergabe.
